text: Baroness Olga Vadimovna von Root (2 December 1901 – 28 June 1967) was a Russian stage actress and singer born in Sevastopol, Crimea. She was the daughter of Baron Vadim Nikolayevich von Root, a Czarist military officer and nobleman, and Lubov Karlovna Kostsyushko-Valyuzhinich, a member of a Polish landed gentry family. Her paternal ancestors were Volga German nobility who came to the Russian Empire during the reign of Peter the Great to serve in the Imperial Russian Army. Her maternal grandfather, Karl Kazimirovich Kostsyushko-Valyuzhinich, was Catholic and the founder of the Archeological Museum in Chersonesus, and her maternal grandmother, Maria Pavlovna Reveliotis, was a Russian Orthodox woman of Greek descent and the granddaughter of General Theodosios Reveliotis, a leader of the Greek War of Independence. Through her mother, Root was also a descendant of the Polish national hero Tadeusz Kościuszko. Root was educated at the Smolny Institute of Noble Maidens in Saint Petersburg, where she trained as a singer. At the age of fifteen, she ran away and performed with a troop of Romani performers, learning their music and dances from Nikolai Kroutchine, after which she was found and returned to her family. During the October Revolution, her family moved from Moscow to Kyiv; her father, loyal to Nicholas II, commanded troops in the White Army. To support her family, Root began singing in cabarets and nightclubs. She was arrested by Bolsheviks during a raid, imprisoned, and ordered to be executed, but her life was spared after a Bolshevik colonel recognized her from the stage and released her. The colonel later spared her mother and siblings from arrest and informed Root that her father would be granted amnesty if he defected to the Red Army. She wrote to her father and persuaded him to switch sides, after which he became an instructor at the Soviety Military Academy. During the rise of Communism, Root became a star of the stage as a singer and actress, performing under the name Olga Vadina and becoming one of the top stars of post-Revolutionary Russia's concert theatre, eventually marrying her manager. She performed a program of Romani ballads at a theatre in Paris and later performed in other European capitals. While living in New York City with her second husband, Armand Hammer, she worked with a musician to transcribe Russian and Romani music. In 1925, while performing in Yalta, she was introduced to Armand Hammer, a Jewish-American millionaire industrialist, and the two fell in love. She obtained a divorce from her first husband in Moscow and married Hammer in a civil ceremony in 1927. They had one son, Julian Armand Hammer, born in Moscow in 1928. The family left Moscow in 1930 and settled on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. They divorced in 1943. Root is the grandmother of American businessman Michael Armand Hammer and the great-grandmother of American actor Armie Hammer.
